title: Hosea Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hosea chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hosea Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hosea Chapter 7.

questions.question: According to Hosea 7:1, what was discovered when God would have healed Israel?
options: The iniquity of Ephraim and the wickedness of Samaria
questions.correctAnswer: The iniquity of Ephraim and the wickedness of Samaria
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:1 states that when God would have healed Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim and the wickedness of Samaria were discovered.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 7:2 says that the people consider in their hearts that God remembers all their wickedness.
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:2 states they do not consider in their hearts that God remembers all their wickedness.

questions.question: Who do the people make glad with their wickedness according to Hosea 7:3?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:3 says they make the king glad with their wickedness.

questions.question: In Hosea 7:4, what are the people compared to?
options: An oven heated by the baker
questions.correctAnswer: An oven heated by the baker
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:4 compares the people to an oven heated by the baker.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 7:5 describes the princes making the king strong with bottles of wine.
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:5 states the princes made the king sick with bottles of wine.

questions.question: What happens to the baker in Hosea 7:6 during the night?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:6 says the baker sleepeth all the night.

questions.question: According to Hosea 7:7, what have the people devoured?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:7 says they have devoured their judges.

questions.question: Which phrase best describes Ephraim in Hosea 7:8?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:8 describes Ephraim as a cake not turned.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 7:9 reveals Ephraim is aware that strangers have devoured his strength.
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:9 states Ephraim knoweth it not.

questions.question: What does the pride of Israel do according to Hosea 7:10?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:10 says the pride of Israel testifieth to his face.

questions.question: In Hosea 7:11, Ephraim is likened to what kind of bird?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:11 compares Ephraim to a silly dove without heart.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 7:12 describes God spreading a net upon the people when they go to Egypt and Assyria.
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:12 states God will spread his net upon them when they go.

questions.question: What reason is given in Hosea 7:13 for the woe and destruction upon the people?
options: Because they fled from God and transgressed against Him
questions.correctAnswer: Because they fled from God and transgressed against Him
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:13 says woe is unto them because they fled from God and transgressed against Him.

questions.question: According to Hosea 7:14, what do the people assemble themselves for?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:14 states they assemble themselves for corn and wine.

questions.question: In Hosea 7:16, what are the princes compared to?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:16 compares the princes to a deceitful bow.

medium.title: Hosea Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hosea Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Hosea 7:7, what is the state of Israel's judges and kings?
options: They are strong and faithful servants of God
They are devoured and fallen because they do not call unto God
They have been exalted by the people and praise God
They rule justly and lead the people to repentance
questions.correctAnswer: They are devoured and fallen because they do not call unto God
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:7 explains that Israel's judges have been devoured and all their kings have fallen because none calls unto God, showing their abandonment of divine help.

questions.question: What metaphor does Hosea 7:8 use to describe Ephraim's condition?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 likens Ephraim to 'a cake not turned,' signifying incomplete preparation or corruption, meaning Ephraim is mixed among the peoples and not properly set apart.

questions.question: What does Hosea 7:9 say about Ephraim's awareness of his condition?
options: Ephraim is fully aware and repents
Ephraim is unaware that strangers have devoured his strength
Ephraim has no gray hairs and is youthful
Ephraim rejoices in his strength and wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Ephraim is unaware that strangers have devoured his strength
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:9 states that strangers have devoured Ephraim's strength but he does not know it, even though gray hairs appear, indicating his ignorance of his declining state.

questions.question: How does Hosea 7:10 describe Israel’s attitude toward God despite His dealings with them?
options: They humbly seek God and repent
Their pride testifies against them and they do not return to the LORD
They are faithful and obedient servants
They worship God sincerely and seek His face
questions.correctAnswer: Their pride testifies against them and they do not return to the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 10 reveals that Israel's pride testifies against them and they do not return to the LORD nor seek Him despite God's dealings with them.

questions.question: In Hosea 7:11, Ephraim is compared to which bird, and what is the significance of this comparison?
options: An eagle soaring high, symbolizing strength
A silly dove without heart, indicating foolishness and lack of wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: A silly dove without heart, indicating foolishness and lack of wisdom
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:11 compares Ephraim to a silly dove without heart, illustrating their foolishness and lack of understanding as they seek help from Egypt and Assyria instead of God.

questions.question: What consequence does God declare in Hosea 7:12 for Ephraim’s reliance on Egypt and Assyria?
options: God will bless Ephraim with prosperity
God will spread His net and bring Ephraim down
God will grant Ephraim victory over enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God will spread His net and bring Ephraim down
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:12 warns that when Ephraim turns to Egypt and Assyria, God will spread His net upon them and bring them down, chastising them as their congregation has heard.

questions.question: Based on Hosea 7:7-8, what does Israel’s failure to call on God lead to, and how is Ephraim described in this context?
options: Leads to prosperity; Ephraim is a strong fortress
Leads to downfall; Ephraim is mixed among the peoples and incomplete like a cake not turned
Leads to peace; Ephraim is a wise leader
Leads to protection; Ephraim is a shield for the people
questions.correctAnswer: Leads to downfall; Ephraim is mixed among the peoples and incomplete like a cake not turned
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 together show that because none calls on God, Israel falls, and Ephraim is described as mixed among peoples and like a cake not turned, symbolizing instability and incompleteness.

questions.question: What does Hosea 7:9-10 teach about the relationship between pride and spiritual blindness in Israel?
options: Pride leads to humility and repentance
Pride testifies to their face and they do not return to God, showing spiritual blindness
Pride has no impact on their spiritual state
questions.correctAnswer: Pride testifies to their face and they do not return to God, showing spiritual blindness
questions.explanation: Verses 9-10 show that despite clear signs of weakness and aging, Israel’s pride prevents them from recognizing their condition and returning to God, illustrating spiritual blindness.

questions.question: According to Hosea 7:11-12, what is the practical lesson about trusting in human alliances instead of God?
options: Trusting in human alliances brings security and peace
Trusting in Egypt and Assyria leads to God's judgment and downfall
Alliances with other nations are encouraged by God
God is indifferent to whom Israel trusts
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting in Egypt and Assyria leads to God's judgment and downfall
questions.explanation: Verses 11-12 warn that Ephraim’s reliance on Egypt and Assyria is foolish and will result in God spreading His net and bringing them down, teaching the importance of trusting God alone.

questions.question: How does Hosea 7:7-9 illustrate the consequences of failing to seek God in leadership and strength?
options: Judges are devoured, kings have fallen, and strength is devoured by strangers
Strength is increased by foreign alliances
questions.correctAnswer: Judges are devoured, kings have fallen, and strength is devoured by strangers
questions.explanation: These verses reveal that without seeking God, Israel’s leadership collapses and their strength is consumed by strangers, demonstrating the cost of neglecting God.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 7:10 states that Israel humbly returns to the LORD and seeks Him after recognizing their pride.
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:10 clearly states that despite Israel’s pride testifying against them, they do not return to the LORD nor seek Him, showing their continued rebellion.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 7:11 compares Ephraim to a silly dove without heart, highlighting their foolishness in seeking help from other nations.
questions.explanation: Verse 11 uses the metaphor of a silly dove without heart to describe Ephraim’s foolishness in calling to Egypt and going to Assyria instead of trusting God.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 7:12 promises that God will bless those who seek help from Egypt and Assyria.
questions.explanation: Contrary to blessing, Hosea 7:12 warns that God will spread His net and bring down those who turn to Egypt and Assyria, showing that such reliance brings judgment.

questions.question: What spiritual truth about repentance and consequences can be learned from Hosea 7:13-14?
options: Despite redemption, Israel transgresses and does not truly cry out to God, leading to destruction
God ignores transgressions once redemption is given
Rebellion against God has no consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Despite redemption, Israel transgresses and does not truly cry out to God, leading to destruction
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 teach that even after being redeemed, Israel transgressed and failed to cry out to God with their heart, resulting in judgment and rebellion consequences.

questions.question: How does Hosea 7:15-16 describe Israel’s attitude and the outcome for their princes?
options: They trust God fully and their princes are preserved
They imagine mischief against God, and their princes will fall by the sword
They live in peace and prosperity
They humble themselves and lead the people rightly
questions.correctAnswer: They imagine mischief against God, and their princes will fall by the sword
questions.explanation: Verses 15-16 indicate that despite God's strengthening, Israel imagines mischief against Him, and their princes will fall by the sword due to their rage and deceitfulness.

hard.title: Hosea Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hosea Chapter 7.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Hosea 7:13 for the woe and destruction pronounced upon Israel?
options: They have fled from God and transgressed against Him
They have trusted in Egypt and Assyria
They have not kept the Sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: They have fled from God and transgressed against Him
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:13 states that the woe and destruction come because Israel has fled from God and transgressed against Him, despite being redeemed.

questions.question: According to Hosea 7:14, how do Israel's people fail to seek God despite their distress?
options: They do not cry to God with their heart
They offer sacrifices to other gods
They pray only in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: They do not cry to God with their heart
questions.explanation: Verse 14 explains that although Israel howled upon their beds, they did not cry to God sincerely with their hearts; instead, they rebelled and assembled for corn and wine.

questions.question: What metaphor does Hosea 7:16 use to describe Israel’s return to their ways, and what is the consequence foretold?
options: A deceitful bow; princes shall fall by the sword
A broken reed; kings shall be humbled
A sinking ship; judges shall perish
A burning flame; people shall be scattered
questions.correctAnswer: A deceitful bow; princes shall fall by the sword
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:16 describes Israel as a deceitful bow and warns that their princes will fall by the sword due to their tongue's rage, resulting in derision in Egypt.

questions.question: Which nations are mentioned in Hosea 7:11 as places Israel turns to for help?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:11 states that Ephraim (Israel) is like a silly dove, calling to Egypt and going to Assyria for help, illustrating their political alliances rather than reliance on God.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'oven' in Hosea 7:4 and 7:6 symbolize in the context of the chapter?
options: The heated anger and corruption of Israel
The warmth of God's protective love
The purification by fire and judgment
The bread of life given by God
questions.correctAnswer: The heated anger and corruption of Israel
questions.explanation: The term 'oven' metaphorically represents the heated anger and internal corruption of Israel, as seen in verses 4 and 6 where it describes their adulterous and deceitful nature.

questions.question: How does Hosea 7:9 describe Israel’s condition despite their awareness?
options: Strangers have devoured their strength, yet they know it not
They are prosperous and have many allies
They have repented and returned to God
questions.correctAnswer: Strangers have devoured their strength, yet they know it not
questions.explanation: Verse 9 states that strangers have consumed Israel’s strength and although there are gray hairs upon them (signs of aging and experience), they do not recognize their condition.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage parallels the theme of Israel’s unfaithfulness and God’s call to repentance found in Hosea 7:13-14?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 2:13 similarly speaks of Israel forsaking God, the fountain of living waters, and digging broken cisterns, paralleling Hosea’s depiction of apostasy and rebellion.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Hosea 7:8 with the phrase 'Ephraim is a cake not turned'?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:8 uses a simile comparing Ephraim to an unturned cake, illustrating incompleteness and imperfection in mixing among the peoples.

questions.question: According to Hosea 7:15, how does Israel respond to God’s strengthening and binding of their arms?
questions.explanation: Verse 15 explains that although God has strengthened Israel’s arms, they still conceive evil plans against Him, showing continued rebellion.

questions.question: What historical context helps explain Israel’s alliances with Egypt and Assyria as criticized in Hosea 7:11?
options: Israel sought military alliances to protect against Assyrian invasion
Israel was expanding its territory peacefully
Israel was isolated and had no foreign contacts
Israel was primarily a sea-faring nation
questions.correctAnswer: Israel sought military alliances to protect against Assyrian invasion
questions.explanation: Historically, Israel’s political strategy involved alliances with Egypt and Assyria for protection; Hosea criticizes this reliance as faithlessness rather than trusting God.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of deceitfulness and unfaithfulness seen in Hosea 7:16?
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:27 condemns hypocrisy and deceit, like Hosea’s metaphor of a deceitful bow, highlighting unfaithfulness to God’s covenant.

questions.question: In Hosea 7:3, what effect do Israel’s wickedness and lies have on their leaders?
options: They make the king glad and the princes happy
They cause the king to mourn and the princes to despair
They lead the king to seek God
They inspire the princes to repent
questions.correctAnswer: They make the king glad and the princes happy
questions.explanation: Verse 3 reveals the irony that Israel’s wickedness and lies actually bring pleasure to the king and princes, showing corruption at all levels of leadership.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 7:12 predicts God will use a net to capture and chastise Israel like birds of the heaven.
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:12 uses the metaphor of God spreading a net to bring Israel down like birds of the heaven, indicating divine judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 7:10 indicates Israel humbly returns and seeks the Lord after recognizing their pride.
questions.explanation: Verse 10 states that despite Israel's pride testifying against them, they do not return to the LORD nor seek Him.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'though I have redeemed them, yet they have spoken lies against me' in Hosea 7:13 in a theological context?
options: It shows Israel’s ingratitude despite God’s salvation
It indicates Israel’s complete ignorance of God
It predicts their total destruction without hope
It affirms Israel’s faithfulness to God
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Israel’s ingratitude despite God’s salvation
questions.explanation: This phrase emphasizes Israel's betrayal and ingratitude despite being redeemed by God, highlighting the theme of covenant unfaithfulness.

theological.title: Hosea Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hosea Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Hosea 7:1 reveal about the state of Israel's iniquity?
options: It was acknowledged by the people
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:1 states that the iniquity of Ephraim was discovered when God sought to heal Israel, indicating that their sins were known and not hidden from Him.

questions.question: According to Hosea 7:3, what do the people make the king glad with?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:3 explicitly states that the people make the king glad with their wickedness and the princes with their lies, highlighting their deceitful nature.

questions.question: What metaphor does Hosea use in 7:4 to describe the people of Israel?
questions.explanation: In Hosea 7:4, Israel is metaphorically described as adulterers, comparing them to an oven heated by the baker, indicating their unfaithfulness and readiness for sin.

questions.question: What is indicated by the phrase 'Ephraim is a cake not turned' in Hosea 7:8?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:8 uses the metaphor of a cake not turned to signify that Ephraim is incomplete and lacking in proper preparation, symbolizing their unwholesome state.

questions.question: What does Hosea 7:10 reveal about Israel's relationship with God?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:10 indicates that despite their pride, they do not return to the Lord their God nor seek Him, illustrating their spiritual apathy.

questions.question: In Hosea 7:11, how is Ephraim described?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:11 describes Ephraim as a silly dove without heart, indicating their foolishness and lack of discernment in seeking help from Egypt and Assyria.

questions.question: What does God promise in Hosea 7:12 regarding those who flee from Him?
options: He will spread His net upon them
He will provide for their needs
questions.correctAnswer: He will spread His net upon them
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:12 indicates that God will spread His net upon those who flee from Him, signifying judgment and capture for their disobedience.

questions.question: What does Hosea 7:13 highlight about Israel's response to God?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:13 laments that Israel has fled from God, indicating their rejection of His sovereignty and the consequences of their transgressions.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is revealed in Hosea 7:14 regarding Israel's cries?
questions.explanation: In Hosea 7:14, God's expectation for sincere cries indicates His mercy, as He desires His people to genuinely seek Him even when they are suffering.

questions.question: What does Hosea 7:15 reveal about God's past actions towards Israel?
options: He has bound and strengthened their arms
questions.correctAnswer: He has bound and strengthened their arms
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:15 states that God has bound and strengthened their arms, signifying His past help and support despite their continued rebellion against Him.

questions.question: What does the imagery of a 'deceitful bow' in Hosea 7:16 suggest about Israel's leaders?
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:16 describes Israel's leaders as a deceitful bow, implying that they are unreliable and will ultimately fall, illustrating their failure to lead righteously.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 6-7 convey about Israel's moral state?
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 illustrate that Israel's moral state is one of judgment readiness, as they are likened to an oven consuming their judges and kings, emphasizing their corruption.

questions.question: What doctrinal theme is highlighted in the combination of verses 2 and 10?
questions.explanation: The combination of verses 2 and 10 highlights God's omniscience, as He remembers all their wickedness and sees their pride, despite their refusal to return to Him.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not intervene in human affairs. What does Hosea 7:12-13 actually teach?
options: God actively judges and chastises His people
God does not care about the nations
questions.correctAnswer: God actively judges and chastises His people
questions.explanation: Hosea 7:12-13 illustrates God's active role in judging and chastising Israel for their transgressions, countering the sceptical claim of divine indifference.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'when I would have healed Israel' in Hosea 7:1?
options: It shows God's desire for restoration
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God's desire for restoration
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates God's desire to heal and restore Israel, reflecting His love and longing for His people to turn from their iniquity.
